newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel monopoly may end sooner - paper.
newsitem.headline: SingTel monopoly may end sooner - paper.

text.p: Singapore Telecom (SingTel) may end its monopoly in basic telecommunication services sooner than the year 2000, the Business Times (BT) newspaper said on Tuesday.

The BT said Singapore was one of four countries which made improved offers to further liberalise telecommunications services at a meeting on the sidelines of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) conference on Monday.
Details of the improved offer are expected to be announced by Singapore Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan on Wednesday, said the paper.
It added that some U.S. officials indicated they might call for Singapore's monopoly to expire two years before the 2000 deadline.
In May, Mah announced that Singapore would end SingTel's monopoly in basic services on April 1, 2000, seven years ahead of an earlier stipulated date.
The telecoms meeting on Monday was attended by 32 countries, said U.S. Acting Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky at a press conference.
The newspaper said according to Barshefsky, who chaired the closed-door meeting, three or four countries had indicated improved offers although she did not name the countries.
Conference sources said besides Singapore, South Korea, Canada and Australia, also indicated enhanced offers.
Experts said that annual global telecom revenues could more than double from the current estimated US$500 billion with liberalisation.
Members of the WTO are in Singapore this week for their first ministerial conference.
